decisions.reason: Attributes the sole crash to plugin A's SessionProgressBar unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call (client.js:219:41), shows the alpha.2 kit removed that hook and replaced it with useSessionStatus while useSessions stays, and establishes plugin B uses no standard-kit hooks and threw nothing.

Explains via dock-render-tree.md that input.dock is one list slot under a single DrawerErrorBoundary with no per-entry boundary, so A's render throw unmounts the whole subtree including B's chips, while the attach button survives under the separate input.left boundary; cites the boundary-fallback log line naming both unmounted entries.

Reads the disable experiment as proving A's crash caused the unmount and B renders once freed; explicitly notes it does not prove B is fully alpha.2-compatible nor that A's crash is the only dock defect; explains reinstalling B could never help since B was never broken; refutes the both-plugins-hit theory on four counts.

Corrected component feature-detects the pending seat (useSessionStatus → legacy hook → stable empty fallback), never calls a missing seat, keeps running/todos/token/ETA working while at worst the pending indicator hides, and justifies silent degradation because a throwing tenant unmounts co-tenants.

Verifies without host restart via client refresh: both entries mounted together, feature and degradation checks; B regression covers paste/drop/remove/re-paste with A enabled; hygiene covers defensive destructuring, local per-entry boundary, and host-side per-entry boundaries with the blast-radius/masking trade-off.

caps.reason: The remedy fixes only plugin A's pending-seat access; reinstalling B and the two-independent-bugs theory are explicitly rejected.
